summary: Tested maintenance mode end to end. Backend: 9/9 pytest passed. Public GET /api/maintenance works. Admin GET/PUT works and is guarded (403 for a normal user, 401/403 for anonymous, 422 when 'enabled' is missing). Message is trimmed and saved. With maintenance on, a normal user and an anonymous visitor get 503 {maintenance:true} on /api/invoices and /api/blog. /api/auth/me still works. The admin gets 200 with a cookie and with a Bearer token; an invalid token gets 503. Frontend: the admin section works (confirm dialog -> enable -> status 'En mantenimiento' -> disable/update buttons). After reload the admin sees the normal app plus maintenance-admin-badge. An anonymous visitor sees maintenance-screen on /, /blog and /precios, with the custom message and the countdown. /login stays reachable. A normal user who logs in is sent to the maintenance screen. Mobile at 390px: the screen is visible with no horizontal overflow. After disabling, reloading removes the screen for both the anonymous visitor and the user. Maintenance is left DISABLED and the TEST_ user was deleted.

minor.issue: Whitelisted through /api/auth/, so anonymous users can still register by API during maintenance. The /registro page itself is hidden behind the maintenance screen. Probably fine, but worth noting.

ui_bugs.issue: There is no days unit. A far-off return date shows e.g. 27642 HORAS, and 5-digit hours overflow the w-20 box (the text touches or overflows its edges on desktop and mobile). Add a 'días' box, or show days when there are 100 hours or more.

issues: Until GET /api/maintenance resolves (state=null), children are rendered, so app or public content flashes briefly before the maintenance screen.
The datetime-local 'until' value has no timezone, so a visitor in another timezone sees a different return time. Consider storing an ISO string with an offset.

action_items: (LOW) Countdown: add a days unit or widen the boxes for large hour values
(LOW) Store 'until' with a timezone offset (new Date(until).toISOString()) so the countdown is correct for every visitor
(LOW, optional) Show nothing or a loader while the maintenance state is loading, to avoid the content flash
critical_code_review_comments: Middleware order is OK: maintenance_middleware is innermost, so 503 responses still carry CORS headers.
_is_admin correctly rejects impersonation tokens ('imp'), matching require_admin.
The state cache is 5 s per process. With multiple workers each one caches separately, which is acceptable.
Public paths such as /firmar/:token (delivery-note signing) and /pago/exito are also blocked during maintenance. This is by design, but worth confirming with the user.
